correctness.rationale: For 2<=k<=n-2 over C, Cauchy–Binet identifies Σ p_I² with det(AA^T). On chart A=[I B], d(det G)/d b_ij=2(adj(G)B)_ij; adj(G)=det G I−adj(G)BB^T shows equality of the Jacobian ideal (det G and derivatives) with entries of adj(G), not merely equality of radicals. Thus singular locus scheme has rad dimension >=2. For exact rad dimension r, choose isotropic R in OGr(r,n), dimension r(n-r)-r(r+1)/2, and a nondegenerate (k-r)-plane in R^perp/R, dimension (k-r)(n-k-r); total Grassmann codim r(r+1)/2, hence 3 at r=2. Deformation of symmetric restricted Gram is submersive in normal coordinates and Schur complement yields transverse det Sym_2=ac-b² A1, plus higher-radical degeneration to r2. OGr(2,n) irreducible for n>=5; n4,k2 splits into two P1 components. Source SymPy script independently inspected and dimension arithmetic rechecked for n<=11; universal argument is symbolic.
